title: Task Analysis
body:
**Task analysis** describes what the user is trying to accomplish, broken into the steps they
actually perform, in the order they perform them.

It is done by watching, because people describe what they are supposed to do and then perform
something else. The description omits the workaround, the second system they have open, and the
note written on paper because the software makes that field hard to reach.

```
Task: admit a patient

  1. confirm identity against the wristband
  2. open the record                      ← 4 clicks, and it fails if the ward is wrong
  3. copy the allergy list from the referral    ← retyped, because it cannot be pasted
  4. record the vitals
  5. print the label                      ← done twice, because the first print is unreliable
```

The analysis produces the design requirements directly. Steps 3 and 5 in that example are
software failures visible only by observation, and no interview would have surfaced either,
since the user has stopped noticing them.

It also reveals mismatches of granularity. A task the software treats as one operation may be
five to the person, or two operations always performed together may be on separate screens. The
interface should follow the task, so the analysis comes before the design, and it feeds the
[[User Persona]] and the [[Prototyping]] that follow.

[[Software Requirements Analysis]] in
[[INTRODUCTION TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING]] is the same activity at the scale of a
whole system.
